findings.issue_text: cook_method: raw_html stores and renders remote content as raw HTML, bypassing Discourse's sanitization pipeline; RSS/embedded content (third-party, partly attacker-influenced) is served back via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb, enabling stored XSS across all embedding sites

TopicEmbed#import interpolates url directly into the HTML of the imported_from footer ("#{url}") without escaping; a URL containing quotes/breakout characters injects arbitrary markup into the post since the regex only checks it starts with http(s)://

embed.js origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring match rather than strict equality; any origin whose string appears within discourseUrl (or protocol/port variations) passes — should compare against the parsed iframe origin exactly

embed/best.html.erb uses `<%- end if %>` which is invalid Ruby/ERB (an `end` followed by a dangling `if` modifier with no condition); the view fails to compile at render time and should be `<%- end %>` with the presence check moved into the initial conditional

layouts/embed.html.erb `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` throws / sends to an empty target origin when the referer is blank or contains quote characters; the referer is also unescaped ERB output into a JS string context

poll_feed.rb `i.content` may be nil for feed items without content, causing NoMethodError (nil.scrub); `i.title` is also passed through unvalidated, and a single malformed item aborts the entire feed poll

poll_feed.rb / topic_retriever.rb `open(...)` on remote URLs has no timeout and no error handling; with retry: false a hung or failing fetch silently kills the scheduled job and blocks all subsequent items — wrap in per-item error handling and set open timeouts
topic_retriever.rb fetch_http calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking presence; when only embeddable_host is configured, a valid embed request raises NoMethodError on nil

TopicEmbed two concurrent retrievals of the same embed_url race on TopicEmbed.create!; the unique index on embed_url makes the loser raise RecordNotUnique, failing the job/transaction — needs rescue/re-lookup or upsert handling

topic_retriever.rb $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire is non-atomic; if the process dies between the two calls the throttle key persists forever and the URL is never retrieved again — use a single `set ... ex: 60, nx: true`

embed_controller.rb referer check breaks embedding for any visitor whose browser suppresses the Referer header (privacy modes, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, HTTPS→HTTP), returning an error page inside the iframe; security relies solely on a client-controlled header

TopicEmbed absolutize_urls port logic assumes port 80 ⇒ http and 443 ⇒ https; URLs like https://host:80/ get the port stripped incorrectly, and scheme-relative (//host/path) or query-relative hrefs are left unabsolutized

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adding force: true to an unrelated create_table will silently drop and recreate the existing top_topics table (destroying data) on environments that already have it

no specs cover sanitization/escaping of imported content — no tests asserting malicious URLs/HTML in feed content are neutralized, nor any controller test for what an attacker-supplied embed_url produces

embed_by_username and embeddable_host lack descriptions in site_settings.yml while other settings document themselves; also no docs for the cook_method: raw_html security implication in the Post.cook_methods comment ("skip the rendering pipeline" understates that sanitization is skipped)

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method: raw_html stores and renders remote content as raw HTML, bypassing Discourse's sanitization pipeline; RSS/embedded content (third-party, partly attacker-influenced) is served back via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb, enabling stored XSS across all embedding sites

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == ...` (app/models/post.rb), explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` using content from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse` and `i.content`/`i.title`) or remote HTML (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses Readability but still outputs HTML). The embed UI then renders that content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Since `post.cooked == post.raw` for raw_html (per `Post#cook`), attacker-influenced feed/remote content can be stored and served as raw HTML, enabling stored XSS in the embed page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed#import interpolates url directly into the HTML of the imported_from footer ("#{url}") without escaping; a URL containing quotes/breakout characters injects arbitrary markup into the post since the regex only checks it starts with http(s)://

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the footer HTML is built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. A crafted URL like `http://x.com' onclick='alert(1)` still matches and would break out of the single-quoted href attribute and inject arbitrary markup/JS into `contents`. Because the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, the injected HTML is not escaped/sanitized and will be rendered (`raw post.cooked` in embed view).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb / topic_retriever.rb `open(...)` on remote URLs has no timeout and no error handling; with retry: false a hung or failing fetch silently kills the scheduled job and blocks all subsequent items — wrap in per-item error handling and set open timeouts

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` and no rescue; in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, remote content is fetched via `open(url).read` similarly without timeouts/handling, and `lib/topic_retriever.rb` calls this. Given `Jobs::PollFeed` sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any exception during fetch/parse will fail the scheduled job with no retry, and a hung `open` can block the job execution entirely. The diff introduces these remote fetches, so the reliability issue is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb fetch_http calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking presence; when only embeddable_host is configured, a valid embed request raises NoMethodError on nil

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, fetch_http does `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` with no presence guard. TopicRetriever#retrieve can be invoked when only `embeddable_host` is set (invalid_host? passes) and `embed_by_username` is blank/nil (EmbedController#best/Jobs::RetrieveTopic do not require it). In that case, `nil.downcase` will raise NoMethodError, breaking valid embed requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed two concurrent retrievals of the same embed_url race on TopicEmbed.create!; the unique index on embed_url makes the loser raise RecordNotUnique, failing the job/transaction — needs rescue/re-lookup or upsert handling

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a pre-check `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. With concurrent imports of the same `embed_url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and then both attempt `create!`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, so the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent), and there is no rescue/re-lookup/upsert handling in the diff, which can fail the job/transaction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire is non-atomic; if the process dies between the two calls the throttle key persists forever and the URL is never retrieved again — use a single `set ... ex: 60, nx: true`

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterwards given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is interrupted between these two calls, the key can remain without an expiration, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely and preventing future retrievals for that embed_url. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff; using a single atomic SET with NX+EX (or equivalent) would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb referer check breaks embedding for any visitor whose browser suppresses the Referer header (privacy modes, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, HTTPS→HTTP), returning an error page inside the iframe; security relies solely on a client-controlled header

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#ensure_embeddable hard-requires a Referer host match: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` raises when `request.referer` is nil/blank, so embedding fails for clients that omit/suppress the Referer header (the spec even asserts this behavior). Additionally, this is the only access control before setting `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`, and it relies on `request.referer` (HTTP Referer header), which is client-supplied and can be absent or forged outside normal browser embedding, making the protection weak.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed absolutize_urls port logic assumes port 80 ⇒ http and 443 ⇒ https; URLs like https://host:80/ get the port stripped incorrectly, and scheme-relative (//host/path) or query-relative hrefs are left unabsolutized

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix-building logic drops the port whenever `uri.port` is 80 or 443, regardless of scheme: `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. For a URL like `https://host:80/...`, `uri.port` is 80 so `:80` is incorrectly omitted, producing wrong absolutized links. Also, the method treats any `href/src` starting with `/` as root-relative; scheme-relative URLs like `//cdn.com/x` also start with `/` and will be rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.com/x`, which is incorrect (and query-relative `?q=1` is left unchanged).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb adding force: true to an unrelated create_table will silently drop and recreate the existing top_topics table (destroying data) on environments that already have it

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. While this migration normally runs only once (so a typical `db:migrate` on an already-migrated environment won’t re-execute it), modifying an old migration to include `force: true` does introduce a real data-loss risk in workflows where the migration is re-run (e.g., migrate:redo/rollback+reapply, or running migrations on a DB that already has `top_topics`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: no specs cover sanitization/escaping of imported content — no tests asserting malicious URLs/HTML in feed content are neutralized, nor any controller test for what an attacker-supplied embed_url produces

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from external RSS/remote HTML with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. That content is then rendered in `embed/best.html.erb` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no sanitization step in `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` (it only absolutizes URLs), and the added specs even assert `post.cooked == post.raw`, implying unescaped HTML is expected. This is a verifiable security defect (XSS risk from attacker-controlled feed/article HTML), and the finding about missing tests for neutralizing malicious HTML/URLs is consistent with the diff because no such tests exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_by_username and embeddable_host lack descriptions in site_settings.yml while other settings document themselves; also no docs for the cook_method: raw_html security implication in the Post.cook_methods comment ("skip the rendering pipeline" understates that sanitization is skipped)

adjudication.rationale: The claim that `embeddable_host` / `embed_by_username` “lack descriptions” in `config/site_settings.yml` is not supported by the diff: this file only defines defaults/groups, while the human-facing descriptions for these settings were added in `config/locales/server.en.yml` (`site_settings: embeddable_host`, `embed_by_username`, etc.). However, the second part is diff-grounded: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, which bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the comment only says it “skip[s] the rendering pipeline” without calling out the security implications—worth clarifying given this is used for imported feed/remote content (`TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: :raw_html`).
